researched_by: the Authority's own car parks page
policy_summary:
The clearest split between parking and sleeping found anywhere so far. At car parks on the higher tariff, GBP10 buys you an overnight stay for the VEHICLE - cars and motorhomes may be parked and left overnight - but camping and overnighting IN a motorhome is explicitly not allowed. Other car parks carry a flat 'no overnight parking'.

So a walker doing the Pennine Way or the Cheviots can legitimately leave a van for GBP10 a night. Someone wanting to sleep in it cannot, at any price. Two different products from the same tariff board, and the distinction is invisible on any competitor's map.
notes: This is the strongest argument yet for the restricts field carrying 'parking' and 'sleeping' separately. A yes/no overnight flag would get this exactly wrong in both directions.
open_questions: Which of the named car parks are on the GBP10 tariff and which carry no overnight parking at all?
Is the sleeping prohibition backed by a byelaw or is it a condition of entry?
Overnight tariff hours - from when to when?

sites.name: Higher-tariff Northumberland NP car parks
sites.notes: GBP10 overnight lets you PARK AND LEAVE a car or motorhome. Sleeping in it is not permitted. Useful for multi-day walks. Day rate is GBP2 per hour to a GBP10 maximum.

sites.name: Overnighting or camping in a vehicle, anywhere in the National Park's car parks
sites.notes: The Authority's wording: camping and overnighting in motorhomes is not allowed. Applies even where the vehicle itself may legitimately be left overnight.

sites.name: Lower-tariff and no-overnight car parks
sites.notes: Several car parks carry a flat 'no overnight parking'. Day rate GBP1 per hour to a GBP6 maximum. The Authority lists car parks including Billsmoor Foot, Buckhams Bridge, Bulby's Wood, College Valley Hillforts, Harehaugh, Hareshaw Linn, Ingram Bridge, Ingram Visitor Centre and Lordenshaws - but does not map tariff to car park in a way that has been captured yet.
